recipes.name: LA galbi (LA style grilled beef short ribs)
ingredients: 3½ pounds (about 1.6 kg) LA-style beef short ribs
⅓ cup water or cooking wine
¼ cup honey (or ⅓ cup brown sugar)
1 Korean pear, or 2 ripe Bosc pears, peeled and cored
A few garlic cloves, thinly sliced
instructions: Trim any excess fat from the short ribs and rinse them a couple of times in cold water.
Soak the ribs in cold water for 10 to 20 minutes to draw out excess blood.
In a large bowl, combine ⅓ cup soy sauce, ⅓ cup water or cooking wine, ¼ cup honey (or ⅓ cup brown sugar), and 1 teaspoon ground black pepper.
Blend 1 Korean pear (about 2 cups when chopped), 8 garlic cloves, 1 medium onion, and 1 teaspoon peeled ginger until smooth and creamy.

Add the blended mixture to the soy sauce mixture. Stir in 2 tablespoons toasted sesame oil. Tip: If you can’t find a Korean pear, use 2 ripe Bosc pears instead. I sometimes use Bosc pears, and they work well!
Rinse the short ribs a couple of times in fresh cold water to remove any remaining bone fragments. Drain well.
Add the ribs to the marinade and mix well with your hands, making sure every piece is coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Overnight is even better because it gives the meat more time to absorb the flavors.

Combine 2 tablespoons soybean paste (doenjang), 1 tablespoon hot pepper paste (gochujang), 1 chopped green onion, 1 minced garlic clove, 1 teaspoon honey, 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl. Mix well.
Rinse and drain the lettuce and perilla leaves. Arrange them on a serving plate or in a basket.
Cut the cucumber into sticks about 3½ to 4 inches (9 to 10 cm) long and ½ inch (1.3 cm) thick. Prepare the carrot the same way, if using.
Chop green chili peppers and slice a few garlic cloves. Arrange them alongside the lettuce and perilla leaves.

Grill, pan-fry, or barbecue the marinated ribs until nicely browned and cooked through on both sides. Because LA galbi is thinly sliced, it cooks much faster than traditional thick-cut ribs, usually in about 5 minutes, depending on the heat and thickness.
Transfer the cooked ribs to a serving plate. Use kitchen scissors to cut the meat away from the bones into bite-sized pieces.

To make a wrap, place a piece of galbi on a lettuce leaf with a perilla leaf. Add a little ssamjang, some sliced garlic, and a piece of green chili pepper. Fold everything into a small bundle and enjoy it in one bite!
